from.place: proof, the kernel of a finite graded free presentation is finitely generated and graded

title: Finite graded generation of kernels over the two-variable polynomial ring
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with the total-degree grading S_d equal to the k-span of monomials of degree d, in the convention [def-sc-p1-standard]. If F and M are finitely generated graded S-modules and q:F \to M is a graded surjection, then ker(q) is a finitely generated graded S-module.

source.place: proof, Noetherianity keeps the successive graded kernels finitely generated

proof.text: Because q is graded, its kernel K=ker(q) is closed under the grading: if an element of K is written as a finite sum of homogeneous components, each homogeneous component also maps to zero under q. Thus K is a graded S-submodule of F.

source.place: proof, the kernel of a graded map is graded

proof.text: The module F is finitely generated and graded by hypothesis, so the graded-submodule finiteness statement [lem-sc-p1-graded-submodule-finite] applies to K and gives that K is finitely generated as a graded S-module.
